rich_text.plain_text: A wall of art works differently to a single print. One piece is a statement; a group is a conversation, and like any conversation it needs someone to lead, a little space between voices, and room for a new one to join later. That is really all a gallery wall is. Here is how to build one that looks collected rather than assembled.

rich_text.plain_text: The most common mistake is hanging pieces too far apart, so the wall reads as scattered prints rather than one group. Keep 5 to 8 cm between frames and hold that gap consistently. Then treat the whole cluster as a single shape: its centre should sit at about 145 cm from the floor, standard eye level, regardless of how large the group grows.

rich_text.plain_text: The best art walls are grown, not bought in an afternoon. Start with three pieces, an anchor and two companions, and leave breathing room at the edges so the arrangement can take a fourth and fifth later. Odd numbers tend to hang together more naturally than even ones, and a new piece is allowed to shift the others; that is the wall living, not a mistake.
